text.en: Asha saw a battery powering a clock and a dye colouring a piece of fabric. She wondered what chemistry could tell her about two such different objects.

Nanochemistry deals with materials of extremely small size, nanoparticles, whose properties differ from those of the same material in bulk. They have many applications, though they also have drawbacks. Pharmaceutical chemistry is about drugs. A pharmaceutical drug is a substance used in medicine to diagnose, prevent or treat a condition, or to affect a body function. Its intended use and risks depend on the particular substance. Anaesthetics cause loss of sensation and antibiotics fight bacteria.
Electrochemistry uses an electrochemical cell, a device in which a chemical change produces electricity or electricity brings about a chemical change. It has two electrodes, the anode and the cathode. Radiochemistry studies radioactive substances and their transformations. During radioactive decay, an unstable nucleus can release radiation and may change into a different nucleus.
Dye chemistry deals with substances that colour materials. Agricultural chemistry looks at fertilisers and pesticides and food chemistry at nutrients and preservatives. Forensic chemists examine evidence from crime scenes using scientific methods.

Applied chemistry asks how chemical ideas explain products, measurements and materials. In this chapter, we compare several fields by the questions they ask.

board.text: Identify the question each field answers

text.en: A nanometre is one billionth of a metre. Particles in the nanoscale range are much smaller than the width of a typical human hair.
Consider a block divided into smaller cubes. The volume stays the same when all pieces are included. Some surfaces that were inside become exposed when we pull the pieces apart.

board.text: Same total volume, greater exposed area

text.en: If all eight smaller cubes have half the edge length, each has one quarter of the original surface area. Eight times one quarter is two, so the combined area doubles.

Some tiny particles can have different optical, electrical or surface properties from a large piece of the same material. Surface area is one reason for differences, and very small sizes can also change physical behaviour.
Chemists study where a material goes during use and disposal as well as how well it works. A useful property does not answer all questions about how a new material should be used.
Pharmaceutical chemistry examines the structure and properties of medicines. Researchers also study how a substance can be prepared and checked for identity and quality under controlled conditions.

board.text: Medicines are studied for identity, quality and effects

text.en: Some medicines are used to reduce pain. Anaesthetics change sensation during a planned medical procedure. These are categories of purpose, and a particular medicine can have additional effects.

board.text: Classification can describe a medicine’s role

text.en: Antibiotics act against susceptible bacteria. Their role differs from medicines used for a viral infection. This is an example of linking a medicine to its target.
In a cell diagram, two electrodes are connected through a path for ions and a separate external path for electrons. Together these paths let a chemical change and an electric current occur.

board.text: Electrodes, ion path and external circuit

text.en: Oxidation happens at the anode. Reduction happens at the cathode. Those terms identify the reaction at each electrode.
In a battery delivering current, a chemical reaction supplies energy to the external circuit. Think of an ordinary cell powering a clock as an example.

board.text: A discharging cell transfers chemical energy to the circuit

text.en: An electrolytic cell uses electrical energy to drive a chemical change. Industrial metal coating is one application. Its energy direction differs from that of a battery delivering current.

board.text: Electrolysis: electrical input drives chemical change

text.en: An isotope is a form of an element with the same proton count and a different neutron count. An isotope with an unstable nucleus is called a radioisotope.
Half-life is the time for half of a large starting population of unstable nuclei to decay on average. Two half-lives leave about one quarter of that population undecayed.

board.text: After two half-lives: ½ × ½ = ¼

text.en: Specialists can detect radiation from certain radioisotopes to follow a substance in a controlled setting. The example illustrates measurement by detection.

board.text: Detection can help follow a tracer

text.en: A dye gives a material colour partly by absorbing some wavelengths of light and allowing others to reach our eyes. How a dye attaches to a fibre also matters.

board.text: Dye colour depends on which light reaches the eye

text.en: A pigment in a paint can be dispersed as small solid particles. A dye is often dissolved when applied. Different products use different ways to hold colour in place.

board.text: A dye and a pigment can carry colour differently

text.en: Agricultural chemistry can compare soil nutrients and how they change. A soil-test result is evidence about the sample, and it helps distinguish a measured shortage from a guess.
Food chemistry studies substances in food and the changes that happen during processing and storage. Some additives affect colour, texture or how long a food retains its quality.

board.text: Food additives can have different functions

text.en: A forensic comparison can check whether two samples have similar properties. A match in colour or one test gives limited evidence. Other observations can add context.

board.text: A single matching feature rarely identifies a sample

text.en: Choose one example such as a battery or a textile dye. Name the chemical idea it uses, then state what observation would help you evaluate it.

problem.en: Why can eight small cubes expose more surface than the single cube from which they were divided?

text.en: Compare the edge lengths. Each small cube has half the original edge length.

why.en: Its surface area is one quarter of the larger cube’s surface area.

text.en: Count eight separate pieces and multiply their surface areas by eight.

why.en: The total exposed surface area doubles while the total volume remains the same.

prompt.en: A friend says Antibiotics are used to cure viral colds. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: They do not cure viral infections.

points.en: Cells have an anode and a cathode.
